newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher after durable goods drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher after durable goods drop.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed to lightly higher on Friday as a surprisingly large drop in U.S. durable goods orders for November dispelled investor fears about an interest rate hike.
Durable goods orders fell 1.6 percent for the month, much larger than the small 0.1 percent rise expected by economists.

The long bond climbed 9/32 to yield 6.56 percent and the March futures contract of the Standard & Poor's 500 Index rose 0.25 to 764.85. Before the release of the data, it had been off about one point.
"The big story is the drop in durable goods orders," said Peter Cardillo, director of research, Westfalia Investments.

"I expect a mixed opening, with bias on the high side due to the strength in bonds but the technology group could go lower at the opening," he said, citing news that Computer Associates would post lower quarterly revenues.

"I think we will trend higher today again, but with the rally at a slower pace compared to yesterday. So we could move into new record territory although it could be a somewhat lacklustre day," he said.
